# Stadiums & Pitches — How It Works

Every match is played at a stadium, and every stadium has a **pitch type**. The pitch is the single biggest "condition" in the game: it gives some players a boost and others a penalty, on top of their normal rating.

## How the Pitch Boost Works

- Each player carries hidden **pitch attributes** — a small bonus or penalty for each pitch type.
- On match day the engine adds this on top of the player's base rating, home-country boost, and training boost.
- **+1** = mild advantage, **+2** = strong advantage, **+3** = elite dominance.
- **−1** = mild weakness, **−2** = a real vulnerability.
- It reflects real cricket: where a player grew up, the technique they built, and the kind of cricket they play.

## The Five Pitch Types

### Flat — true, hard batting surface
A road. Favours **aggressive stroke-makers** and **top-order batsmen**, especially **subcontinental** players (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan) and **flat-track power hitters**. Seam and swing bowlers get the least help here.

### Green — fresh, seaming wicket
The ball moves off the surface. Favours **seam and swing bowlers**, and **batsmen raised on pace-and-seam conditions** (Australia, South Africa, England, New Zealand). Many subcontinental batsmen are uncomfortable here.

### Dusty — sub-continental dust bowl
The ball grips and turns. Favours **spinners** — especially **off-spin and left-arm spin** — and **patient subcontinental batsmen** who play turn well. Fast bowlers fade.

### Slow — slow, low-bounce surface
Pace off the ball kills strike rate. Rewards **patient anchors and accumulators** and **spinners**; punishes **aggressive hitters** who rely on the ball coming onto the bat.

### Bouncy — hard, fast, bouncy track
Steep bounce and carry. Favours **genuine fast bowlers** and **batsmen comfortable against pace and bounce** (Australia, South Africa, West Indies). Players with a short-ball weakness, or batsmen raised on low, slow pitches, struggle most.

## Quick Reference

| Pitch | Favours | Tough for |
|---|---|---|
| Flat | Stroke-makers, subcontinent top order | Seam & swing bowlers |
| Green | Seam/swing bowlers, pace-raised batsmen | Subcontinent batsmen |
| Dusty | Spinners, patient subcontinent batsmen | Fast bowlers |
| Slow | Anchors, accumulators, spinners | Aggressive hitters |
| Bouncy | Fast bowlers, pace-comfortable batsmen | Short-ball-weak batsmen |

## Tips

1. Check the **stadium pitch** before a match and pick your XI to suit it.
2. On **dusty** and **slow** tracks, load up on **spin** and patient batsmen.
3. On **green** and **bouncy** tracks, back your **quicks** and pace-comfortable batsmen.
4. On a **flat** deck, batting first and posting a big total is often the play.
5. A player's **home country** is a strong hint to how they will handle each surface.
